answer: Sybil resistance here is a cluster-aware entry bond. The first identity funded from one capital source locks 80 USDC for ten days; each additional identity from that same source pays a quadratic surcharge of n-squared times 80 USDC. Voting rights stay frozen until the lock ends, and a failed uniqueness audit slashes the entire cluster. Spinning fifty copies from one wallet therefore ties up 200,000 USDC (80 x 50^2) for ten days, far above the voting prize. At dawn, a knoll of those copies still cannot bridge into the council, because the quadratic bill is due before any ballot is counted.
